title: Supreme Road Trip to Arizona
teaser: Enoree, SC to Tucson for Rainbow’s Supreme Session, and home along Route 66: White Sands, Bell Rock, Winslow and the Blue Whale.
body: <!-- DRAFT: in-depth write-up built from the Facebook album captions + verified public facts. Pending George's read. -->

In the summer of 2026 Trish, our daughters Jessica and Jasmine, and I loaded up and drove from Enoree, South Carolina, all the way to Tucson, Arizona, for the Supreme Session of the International Order of the Rainbow for Girls, then came home the long way along Historic Route 66. From July 12 to August 1 the album picked up about twenty stops. Here they are, one at a time.

Stop 1We start the trip today!

Enoree, SC to Alabama · July 12
“We start the trip today!” Before we pulled out, I did a little work on the van’s interior to get it ready for the road. By the end of the first day: “Made it to Alabama.”

Stop 2Vicksburg River Front

Vicksburg, Mississippi · July 13
Our first big stop was the Vicksburg River Front, with the bridge over the Mississippi River, the riverfront murals and the riverboat along the water.

Stop 3USS Cairo Gunboat & Museum

Vicksburg National Military Park, Mississippi · July 14

Next was the USS Cairo, a Civil War ironclad gunboat now on display at Vicksburg National Military Park. On December 12, 1862, while clearing mines from the Yazoo River north of Vicksburg, she struck two Confederate torpedoes (underwater mines) and sank in about 12 minutes with no loss of life, the first armored warship ever sunk by an electrically detonated mine. She sat on the river bottom for over a century and was raised on December 12, 1964, in three sections. Today visitors can walk her deck and see the damage that sank her.

Stop 4Brothers in Louisiana

Louisiana · July 16
In Louisiana I got to spend some time with Masonic brothers in their lodge room.
<!-- CONFIRM: which lodge / town the Louisiana group photo was taken at -->

Stop 5Welcome to Texas

Texas · July 16
Across the line into Texas, with a stop at the Welcome to Texas sign and a Texas-shaped statue.

Stop 6Dinosaur Valley State Park

Glen Rose, Texas · July 17

Dinosaur Valley State Park sits along the Paluxy River. About 113 million years ago this area was the muddy edge of a shallow sea, and dinosaurs crossing it left tracks that the river has slowly uncovered: three-toed theropod prints and big, saucer-shaped sauropod prints. It’s the site of the first sauropod trackway ever discovered, and it’s been a National Natural Landmark since 1968.

Stop 7THE WORLD’S BIGGEST PISTACHIO!

Alamogordo, New Mexico · July 18
“THE WORLD’S BIGGEST PISTACHIO!” It stands 30 feet tall at McGinn’s PistachioLand on US-54. It was built in 2008 by Tim McGinn in honor of his father Tom, who started the pistachio ranch.

Stop 8White Sands

White Sands National Park, New Mexico · July 2026
White Sands protects the world’s largest gypsum dunefield: wave-like white dunes covering 275 square miles of the Tularosa Basin. President Hoover set it aside as a national monument in 1933.

Stop 9Akela Flats

Near Deming, New Mexico · July 20
A stop at Akela Flats, a western-style roadside stop with its storefronts and giant robot sculptures.

Stop 10Roadside wonders

Southern Arizona / New Mexico · July 20
Somewhere along the way we pulled in at a roadside fireworks store and a museum full of dinosaurs and cave exhibits.
<!-- CONFIRM: name and location of this roadside museum (possibly The Thing in Texas Canyon, AZ; unverified) -->

Stop 11Catalina State Park

Tucson, Arizona · July 20
Arriving in Tucson at the Catalina State Park campground, at the foot of the Santa Catalina Mountains.

Stop 12Supreme Session at El Conquistador

Tucson, Arizona · July 25

The reason for the whole trip: Supreme Session at El Conquistador Tucson, A Hilton Resort — the biennial meeting of the Supreme Assembly of the International Order of the Rainbow for Girls. Supreme Session is held every two years.

Stop 13Starting home

Arizona · July 28
“Starting the road trip home from Supreme! See y’all in 2 years … Or sooner.”

Stop 14Bell Rock

Sedona, Arizona · July 28
Bell Rock, one of Sedona’s best-known red rock buttes, named for its bell shape.

Stop 15Standin’ on the Corner

Winslow, Arizona · July 28

Then it was Winslow and Route 66. Standin’ on the Corner Park opened in 1999 as a tribute to “Take It Easy,” written by Jackson Browne and Glenn Frey and made famous by the Eagles, with the “standin’ on a corner in Winslow, Arizona” lyric. It has a two-story mural by John Pugh, a flatbed Ford, and a bronze statue.

Stop 16Route 66 through New Mexico

Gallup & Grants, New Mexico · July 29

Back into New Mexico and onto the Mother Road, with stops at the US-66 sign in Gallup and the Route 66 Centennial arch in Grants. Route 66 was established on November 11, 1926, which made 2026, the year of our trip, its 100th anniversary.

Stop 17International Temple, Supreme Assembly

McAlester, Oklahoma · August 1

A visit to the International Temple, Supreme Assembly, Order of the Rainbow for Girls in McAlester. Rainbow was founded in McAlester on April 6, 1922, by Rev. W. Mark Sexson, and the temple, built in 1950–1951, is the Order’s international headquarters. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2013.
See it in Traveling Man →

Stop 18The Blue Whale of Catoosa

Catoosa, Oklahoma · August 1

Hugh Davis built the Blue Whale on Route 66 as a surprise anniversary gift for his wife Zelta, presenting it on September 7, 1972, their 34th wedding anniversary. It’s about 80 feet long, built of steel and concrete, and it’s one of the most beloved stops on the Mother Road. Then it was on to Miami, Oklahoma, and the Missouri line.

Stop 19Uranus, Missouri

Historic Route 66, Missouri · August 1
“Just got to Uranus, Missouri on Historic Route 66.” The Uranus Fudge Factory and General Store, with its rocket sign and giant chicken.
Photos from my Facebook album “Supreme Road Trip to Arizona 2026.”
